testimonials.heading: MEASURABLE RESULTS
testimonials.pullQuote: The CETé diagnosis identified gaps that our internal audits couldn't see. Our move from BBB to AAA strengthened our credibility with our clients.
testimonials.paragraph1: When we called on CETé, we thought our Live Working management level was satisfactory. Our initial BBB rating revealed a different reality: formally correct procedures, but significant field gaps.
testimonials.paragraph2: The DPS diagnosis highlighted three critical areas: qualification traceability, protective equipment compliance, and above all, the day-to-day safety culture. Issues our internal audits weren't capturing.
testimonials.paragraph3: Over 14 months of Campus CPF support, we restructured our training, deployed field coaching for our Live Working coordinators, and implemented a continuous regulatory monitoring system.
testimonials.paragraph4: The result: a 40% reduction in electrical incidents, measurable upskilling of our teams, and most importantly, the jump from BBB to AAA - a transformation that strengthened our credibility with our clients.

hero.heading: WHO ARE <accent>WE</accent>?
hero.subtitle: From <serect>SERECT</serect> to <cete>CET</cete> - 20 years in the field, a rating agency.
hero.description: Four independent live working (TST) experts from SERECT founded CETé - Consortium Experts Techniques Électricité - to objectively measure electrical risk management with a structured and transparent rating system.

originStory.heading: THE CET<sup>é</sup> CONSORTIUM
originStory.narrative1: In 1962, SERECT was created to promote and develop Live Working (TST) in France. In 2000, EDF generalized TST audits across EDF units on a 4-year cycle. In 2008, visits to ERDF contractor companies began. ENEDIS generalized field audits at their contractor companies in 2014.
originStory.narrative2: In 2019, former SERECT experts founded their consulting firm and created an international observatory for electrical risk management. They identified a gap: no independent rating system existed.
originStory.narrative3: In 2026, they created CETé, a fully independent rating agency with the ambition of becoming the reference electrical risk rating agency in France and internationally, and a recognized influencer in sharing best practices for electrical risk prevention.

vigilance.vulnerabilityDescription: Residual risk exposure when vigilance is insufficient.
vigilance.ncDescription: A few examples of major non-conformities that can result in a D rating on one or more criteria.

items.1: Poor knowledge of the domain framework

items.0: Operator not trained or not retrained
items.1: Operator not qualified for the installation or voltage domain concerned by the worksite

nc2.title: Operational
nc2.intro: Any non-conformity that could have irreversible bodily consequences in the event of equipment or human failure:

items.1: Deliberate deviation observed: failure to wear suitable work clothing, helmet with face shield or live-working gloves
items.2: Failure to respect fundamental trade practices
items.3: No voltage absence testing (VAT), earthing or short-circuiting
items.5: Work started without authorization (client company order, prevention plan, access authorization, work order…)

meta.title: O-M-T Observatory: Live Working Mastery Data
meta.description: The Live Working Mastery Observatory: 133 DPS audits, 43 companies, over 10,000 requirements observed (2022-2025). Field data on electrical risk in France.

hero.heading: THE LIVE WORKING MASTERY OBSERVATORY
hero.description: The field knowledge base that objectively measures how French companies control electrical risk.

observatory.intro: The Live Working Mastery Observatory (O-M-T) is the knowledge base built by CETé since 2022. It capitalises the results of Safety Performance Diagnoses (DPS) conducted with French companies performing live working, in low voltage (LV) and high voltage (HV), to objectify recurring gaps and benchmark each organisation against its sector.

method.heading: Methodology
method.item1: Field audits (DPS) conducted on worksites representative of each company's activity, in both low and high voltage.
method.item2: The AudiMaT cross-analysis: confronting the organisation's self-assessment, its compliance with the professional recommendation, and the technical gestures observed in real situations.
method.item3: An anonymised consolidation of findings, feeding the sector benchmark and the Vigi-Score® rating framework.

tertiles.heading: Three organisation profiles
tertiles.description: The cross-analysis of results reveals three tertiles, from the most exposed to the most mature:
tertiles.t1Desc: Weak safety culture, incomplete documentation, resistance to change. High accident probability.
tertiles.t2Desc: Formal compliance without real ownership, gaps between procedures and field practices. Moderate accident probability.
tertiles.t3Desc: Embedded safety culture, measurable continuous improvement, proactive anticipation. Low accident probability.
tertiles.cta: Where do you stand? Request your assessment

observatory.note: Observatory data is consolidated on an ongoing basis and published in aggregated, anonymised form.
